best_moment.what: The Counter: I told them exactly why the redesign would fail. It felt right to say it, and the ending card later confirmed it was the turning point of the whole career.

worst_moment.what: Indicators again, and I picked the bottom 20th for the fourth time. Same choice, same screen, and nothing ever showed who got the credit.

answer.held_back_by: Telling them straight why the counter would fail at 27. The system apparently wants people who don't say that, so my honesty capped my promotion even though my appraisals were outstanding.
answer.ending_fair_why: The ending card explained the reasons clearly, and being honest and boring-clean fit the character I was playing. I only wish I had been told about the ceiling earlier, though that is probably the point.
answer.chase_next: The Permanent Secretary route: stay in the service, say the safe thing at the Counter, and see whether the top civil service job feels any different from DPM.
answer.play_again_why: I'm done for now. 45 years of taps was a lot, and many years felt similar. Maybe tomorrow, once I want to try the other route.

tone_breaks.line: The Director called the system 'a joke, a game', and winked.
tone_breaks.note: The wink made it unclear whether it was a joke or a real test, and it never paid off, so it felt a bit smug.

tone_breaks.line: Declassified: 'Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.'
tone_breaks.note: Funny, but it was the game talking to me instead of the story, which felt a little knowing.

answer.title_fit_why: I made $35M, but the real story was about whether I got confirmed and what kind of grade I was stuck at, and my STAND score slid while the pay hardly mattered. The pay is just a number, and the career is the actual game.
